categories.main_business_segments: The company operates primarily in four segments: Contact Center Services, IT Services, Display Solution Business, and DX (Digital Transformation) Services. Contact Center Services include consulting, operation, and management of customer contact centers. IT Services cover CDN, system integration (SI), system management (SM), and security solutions. Display Solution involves importing and selling NEC projectors and related equipment. DX Services focus on AI contact center solutions and smart factory solutions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced IT technologies including AI, Big Data, Cloud, Mobile, and IoT for its intelligent contact center and smart factory solutions. It develops proprietary AI engines such as 'Callisto' for speech recognition and natural language processing. The IT segment includes CDN technology for fast and stable content delivery, system integration with hardware like Hitachi servers and Huawei 5G equipment, and endpoint security solutions through partnerships. Display solutions involve importing high-tech projectors and sterilization lamps. The DX segment integrates AI chatbots, voice bots, and machine learning for customer support automation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include financial institutions, public agencies, telecommunications, retail, manufacturing, and online service providers. Major clients for contact center services are Hyundai Card/Capital and Samsung Electronics. IT services target digital native companies such as internet portals, online education, e-commerce, media, and gaming. Display solutions serve enterprises, educational institutions, cinemas, and public organizations. DX services focus on internal Hyosung Group companies and external clients in petrochemicals, semiconductors, steel, and shipbuilding sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in South Korea with a strong domestic market presence. It imports products from Japan (NEC projectors) and partners with global IT firms like Hitachi, Huawei, and Tanium. The smart factory solutions are deployed in Hyosung Group’s factories across China, Vietnam, India, and Brazil. The company also maintains extensive overseas subsidiaries and affiliates in Asia, Europe, and the Americas as part of the Hyosung Group.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates mainly in the midstream and downstream segments of the supply chain. It provides service outsourcing (contact centers), IT system integration, and solution deployment rather than manufacturing. It acts as a distributor for hardware products (e.g., NEC projectors, Hitachi servers, Huawei network equipment) and develops proprietary software solutions. It also functions as a service provider and technology integrator for its clients.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding AI-powered intelligent contact center solutions (AICC), cloud-based contact center platforms, and metaverse-based call center technologies. The company invests in R&D for speech-to-text, text analysis, AI chatbots, and voice bots to enhance customer service automation. It also focuses on smart factory digital transformation using IoT and data analytics platforms. Partnerships with domestic and international tech firms support technology advancement and solution diversification.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through service contracts for contact center outsourcing, IT system integration and management, product sales (projectors and IT hardware), and subscription/license fees for DX solutions. Contact center services are billed monthly based on contracts. CDN services charge usage-based monthly fees. Display solutions are sold through distributors and direct sales. DX services offer both license sales and subscription-based models with additional fees for implementation and maintenance.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company holds a leading market position in the Korean contact center outsourcing industry, competing with other top-tier firms. In IT services, it competes with large system integrators and global CDN providers like Akamai and Amazon. In display solutions, it faces competition from Japanese brands such as Epson, NEC, and Panasonic, as well as emerging Chinese ODM products. The company differentiates itself through accumulated expertise, proprietary AI technologies, and strong partnerships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, the company reported consolidated revenues of approximately 503.8 billion KRW with an operating profit of 19.2 billion KRW, reflecting a slight decline from the previous year. The contact center segment accounts for over 75% of revenue, followed by IT services (13.7%), display solutions (7.4%), and DX services (3.5%). The company has maintained stable capital with no recent changes in capital stock and holds a strong credit rating of A+. It has shown steady growth in contact center services and is expanding its DX business.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company emphasizes its extensive experience and high-quality human resources in contact center operations, combined with advanced AI and cloud technologies to provide flexible, efficient, and secure customer service solutions. Its proprietary AI engine 'Callisto' and integrated intelligent contact center platforms enhance consultation accuracy and reduce costs. The company’s smart factory solutions optimize manufacturing processes through real-time data analytics and AI-powered quality control. Its strong partnerships and comprehensive service offerings create competitive advantages in technology integration and customer satisfaction.
